summary: Plugin that lets AI coding agents design physical parts: they write CAD models in Python, check them for manufacturing and export STEP, STL or 3MF.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: text-to-cad gives coding agents local workflows for designing physical products. Ask your agent for a part or assembly and it writes the model as a Python script with build123d and OpenCASCADE, runs it and shows it in a viewer. It can also design KiCad circuit boards, check whether parts can be machined, cut, molded or 3D printed, run stress checks, produce engineering drawings, make Blender renders and prepare files for fabrication services.
sixtySeconds.problem: CAD tools have a steep learning curve. This lets you describe a part in plain language and get a real, manufacturable model file.
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for code-based, editable CAD models, manufacturing checks and support for over 20 agent apps.
requirements: An agent app such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or Gemini CLI

overview: Run the one-line installer. It installs uv if needed, then the cad command, then the plugin for each agent app it finds, and turns on automatic updates.
Then ask your agent for a part. Outputs include STEP, GLB, STL and 3MF, plus DXF for sheet metal and fabrication files for circuit boards.
It works in Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Cline, Goose, OpenCode, Windsurf and many more. Manual install steps are in docs/install.md. It is MIT licensed.
limitations: Relies on your agent's model quality
